title: Mac video mode: full-Retina resize every tick pins a core and starves the WebUI
description: Found during Aurora-ta5's UI check: after switching Dashboard to Video on Mac, the lights switched but the mode toggle stayed on Audio. Cause, from 'sample' on the live app: ScreenCaptureKit streams at full pixel size (display points x backingScaleFactor, ScreenCaptureKitGrabber.mm configureAndStartStream, e.g. 3420x2214 BGRA), and every tick Orchestrator::_prepareSource INTER_AREA-resizes that on the CPU down to subsampleWidth (16 here): 2349/2360 tick-thread samples in cv::resizeArea_. That overruns even a 60Hz tick, so the process sits at ~105% CPU and the loop never sleeps -- which then triggers the known lock-starvation mechanism, Aurora-cgr (PipelineHost holds m_mutex across the tick; /api/monitors and /api/zones waited 2-30s). DashboardScreen._switchMode re-renders only after _loadAll fetches both, so the toggle looks stuck. Pre-existing; affects real Mac use (CPU/battery), not just the fake stack. Scope here: the Mac trigger -- have SCK deliver a small frame (SCStreamConfiguration width/height near the needed sampling size, GPU-scaled) so a tick fits its budget. The general never-yield/starvation hardening stays in Aurora-cgr; an optimistic mode-toggle render is optional polish.
acceptance_criteria: Mac video mode at 60Hz on a Retina display: process CPU well under one core, /api/monitors and /api/zones respond in <100ms while running, mode toggle updates immediately; parity fixtures unchanged (core path) or deliberately regenerated if resize input changes.
close_reason: SCK frames GPU-scaled via setCaptureWidthHint; CPU 105%->5.5%, API waits 2-30s->1ms; owner confirmed toggle and viz.

title: Mac: minimal .app bundle wrapper for TCC identity
description: Aurora-8mk.4's probe confirmed both a bare Mach-O binary and one with an embedded Info.plist (-sectcreate __TEXT __info_plist) attribute their Screen Recording grant to Terminal, not the binary, when exec'd directly from a shell. Real fix: wrap app/mac's built binary as a minimal .app bundle (Aurora.app/Contents/{Info.plist,MacOS/Aurora}) and launch it via 'open' (or double-click) instead of exec'ing the raw binary, so the launch goes through LaunchServices, which resets the responsible-process chain and makes the bundle itself -- not Terminal -- the attributable process. Free ad-hoc codesign, no Apple Developer account needed (that's Phase 8/notarization only, still deferred). Not tray-parity: no LSUIElement agent style, no NSStatusItem menu, no SMAppService login item yet -- just enough bundle structure for its own TCC identity. See docs/MacSupport.md 'Load-bearing risk' + build-sequencing Phase 3b.
design: CMake post-build step on the mac-app target: create Contents/MacOS + Contents/Info.plist, copy/move the built binary in, ad-hoc codesign (codesign -s -). Keep it minimal -- this is the terminal-only tier's bundle, not tray-parity's.
acceptance_criteria: Rebuild app/mac (or the throwaway probe) as a .app bundle, launch via 'open Aurora.app', confirm System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Screen Recording lists the bundle's own identifier as a distinct entry from Terminal after granting.
close_reason: Verified: wrapped the Aurora-8mk.4 probe as a real .app bundle (tcc-probe-app.app), launched via 'open', and it showed up as its own entry in System Settings -> Screen Recording, not Terminal. app/mac's CMakeLists.txt now builds aurora-app-mac as a MACOSX_BUNDLE target (Aurora.app/Contents/MacOS/Aurora + Info.plist), ad-hoc signed post-build (free, no Apple Developer account). Also picked up a bundle icon (Aurora.icns) built from the existing Linux tray icon set via app/mac/make_icns.sh. Unblocks Aurora-8mk.5.

title: Linux PipeWire capture freezes while a window is fullscreen (GNOME Wayland)
description: Found during Aurora-gj0.3 live validation (2026-09-24, GNOME Wayland, PipewireGrabber via 'linux' input, --fresh vs fake bridge). A maximized Firefox page alternating red/blue every 1.5s was tracked correctly by capture. After F11, capture delivered one correct fullscreen frame (pure red, 1.00/0.04/0.04) and then froze on it for ~18s while the page kept alternating; it resumed as soon as fullscreen was exited. Two earlier kiosk-mode runs froze the same way on Firefox's first paint (constant black, then constant near-white). Hypothesis (unconfirmed): GNOME direct scanout / unredirection of fullscreen windows stops the screencast stream from producing new frames or damage, and the grabber keeps serving its last buffer. This hits the core use case (fullscreen video). Repro harness: the color driver + tools/light-viz-relay/validate.py.

description: Load-bearing risk for the whole tier: TCC attributes a permission request up the launching chain to a 'responsible process', and terminal-launched binaries have been observed landing on the terminal app instead of the child process. Build a throwaway Mach-O binary calling a TCC-gated capture API two ways -- bare, and with an embedded Info.plist/CFBundleIdentifier (-sectcreate __TEXT __info_plist) -- run both from Terminal, and check whether the Screen Recording grant/prompt lands on the binary or on Terminal itself. The embedded-plist variant also derisks the later notarization path (same Info.plist requirement). Can run in parallel with P0-P2, but must resolve before starting the real ScreenCaptureKit grabber work. (docs/MacSupport.md, 'Load-bearing risk' + build-sequencing phase 3).
acceptance_criteria: Clear answer: does an unbundled/bundled probe binary get its own Screen Recording entry in System Settings, or does the grant attach to Terminal/iTerm? Written up in docs/MacSupport.md.
notes: 2026-09-24: attempted to start this while unattended. Two actions in a row got blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier: reading TCC.db directly, and even a routine 'bd update --claim' on this issue. Given the pattern, stopping here rather than probing further -- this needs the user present. See chat for what's actually needed (build the probe binaries, but the System Settings / TCC.db inspection step needs interactive/authorized access this session doesn't have).

title: Phantom 'already running': startup wedges pre-bind while holding the instance lock

title: Shutdown crash: TrayIcon dtor calls get_future on moved-from promise (std::terminate)
description: ~TrayIcon called m_worker->ready.get_future() after ready was moved into the worker thread -> future_error(no associated state) out of noexcept dtor -> terminate on EVERY shutdown. Found via daemon log after user-visible flakiness. Fix: retrieve readyFuture before the move, dtor blocks on it. title: Persisted garbage refreshRate from unreduced PipeWire fraction bricks launch (black screen)
description: User's ~/.config/aurora/config.json contained refreshRate:15729223, nuxCompleted:false, empty activeMonitorName. Chain: PipewireGrabber::displayRefreshRate() returns raw max_framerate.num (unreduced PipeWire fraction numerator) as Hz -> Orchestrator::init derives+persist refreshRate=15729223 -> runtime loop at 15.7M updates/sec hangs daemon -> UI fetchJson (no timeout) hangs forever in bootstrap -> blank/black page on every launch since value is persisted. Empty activeMonitorName is legitimate (means auto/primary per MonitorSelector + RuntimeTests) and NOT the cause. Fixes: (1) reduce num/den fraction in PipewireGrabber::displayRefreshRate with den==0 guard; (2) clamp Config::setRefreshRate upper bound and route ConfigStore::load through setters so persisted garbage self-heals; (3) consider fetchJson timeout so hung daemon shows unreachable message instead of blank.
close_reason: Fixed: PipeWire fraction reduced in displayRefreshRate, refreshRate clamped in setter + sanitized on load (tests green: core 65/65, input/linux 14/14), fetchJson timeout added, lesson filed

title: Hue REST: verify bridge TLS certificate instead of disabling verification
description:
output/hue/src/HttpClient.cpp sets CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER and CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST to false for every bridge REST call, so a LAN man-in-the-middle can impersonate the bridge and read the hue-application-key header. Philips' guidance (and Hyperion 2.2.0, which made it a breaking change) is to validate against the Signify Hue root CA and check that the certificate's CN matches the bridge id.

Reference: hyperion.ng (MIT) ships philips_hue_ca.pem as a resource and checks peer CN against the bridge id in libsrc/leddevice/dev_net/ProviderRestApi.cpp (~509, getAlternateServerIdentity); LedDevicePhilipsHue.cpp has a diyHue carve-out for emulated bridges without a Signify cert.

Open points:
- Bridge id source: discovery response / /api/0/config, stored with the connection.
- tools/fake-hue-bridge serves a self-signed cert: tests need a test CA or an explicit dev-only trust override (never a silent fallback).
- Mac links system libcurl; confirm CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB or a CA file path works on all three platforms.
- Decide diyHue support (explicit opt-in) vs. none.
- Keep the notice if any Hyperion code is ported.
acceptance_criteria: Real bridge: REST calls succeed with verification on. Wrong CN or untrusted cert: call fails with a clear error, no fallback. Fake bridge tests pass via test CA/dev override. Works on Linux, Mac, Windows.

title: Pause/resume streaming without quitting the app
description:
Today the only way to stop lights is /api/stop (or tray Stop), which quits the process, so the WebUI and any external controller (Muse, MCP, MQTT) can stop Aurora but never start it again. Pause = shut down the pipeline (Hue disableStreaming, capture torn down) while the process and HTTP server keep running; resume = reloadPipelineFromDisk. PipelineHost already tolerates a null pipeline (fresh-install idle state), so no IOutput/IInput changes are needed.

1. PipelineHost: pause() (shutdown(false) under the lock, then drop the pipeline) and isPaused(). A settings save while paused writes config but stays paused (no silent restart of lights).
2. Route: PUT /api/state {"running": bool}, idempotent, in core PipelineRoutes -- not copy-pasted per app like /api/stop. Report paused state via /api/capabilities (or the events stream if one exists by then).
3. Pause is in-memory only: a relaunch always resumes.
4. WebUI: Pause/Resume beside Stop on the Dashboard (DashboardScreen.js).
5. Tray: Pause/Resume item on Mac (TrayIcon.mm NSMenu), Windows (AppendMenuA beside IDM_STOP), Linux SNI (with or after Aurora-lx4.2).
6. Tests: pause->resume rebuilds from the same config; pause with no pipeline is a no-op; settings PUT while paused stays paused.

Platform notes:
- Linux Wayland: resume re-enters the screencast portal; IRestoreTokenStore should make it silent. Verify; missing token = dialog, and Aurora-p91 (60s stall on denial) applies.
- Mac: rebuild is cheap with permission granted; the screen-recording indicator clearing while paused is a privacy win worth checking.
- Windows: DXGI rebuild is cheap.
- All: Hue resume needs a fresh DTLS handshake (seconds); Aurora-vf1.1 measures that cost.

Rejected: skip ticks instead of tearing down -- capture and its OS indicator stay live, and the bridge drops the idle stream on timeout anyway.
acceptance_criteria: From WebUI, tray (all three platforms) and PUT /api/state: lights stop and bridge leaves entertainment mode; process and WebUI stay up; resume restores lights with the prior config; Wayland resume shows no portal dialog when a restore token exists; tests in step 6 pass.
notes: 2026-10-02 decisions from [[external-control]]: (1) enforce pause inside PipelineHost::reload, not only the route -- reloadPipelineFromDisk is shared by settings saves, /api/reload and Hue pairing, any of which would otherwise resume; (2) a settings save while paused writes config and stays paused, applied on resume (Hue Sync Box syncActive semantics); (3) a null pipeline blanks Zone Mapping and the monitor picker -- serve zones from ZoneMapStore and monitors from a cached last list while paused. Reference: hyperion.ng component states (LEDDEVICE / ALL enable-disable) keep the instance running.

title: HA prep 8: harden the local API before any HA credential exists
description:
Aurora's REST API has no auth and binds 0.0.0.0. Today the worst case is someone on the LAN changing lights; with an HA token stored it becomes access to the home.
- Origin/Host check on state-changing routes, so web pages can't drive localhost Aurora.
- Rule: secrets are never returned by any route.
- Rule: changing the HA URL clears the stored token, so a LAN client can't point Aurora at a fake HA and have it send the refresh token.
- Decide whether 0.0.0.0 stays the default (WebUI from another device needs it).
Useful now for Hue too.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-origin PUT is rejected in a test; WebUI and demo still work; rules written into [[home-assistant-output]] and the API docs.
close_reason: Origin/Host gate on non-GET routes; secrets rules (no stored secret returned; stored Hue creds bound to stored bridge; repoint clears creds); rules in HomeAssistantOutput.md#local-api-rules + hue README; 0.0.0.0 stays. Verified Linux: AuroraNetworkTests, Hue suite 47 cases; web node tests 12/13 (demo-shim version drift, pre-existing).

The sink field is gated on audioInputs including 'linux-audio', and fetches /api/linux/audio-sinks. NodeGraphPipeline.md's UX section needs sections to follow the active graph (monitor picker iff video capture, sink picker + banner iff audio source, Zone Mapping iff zone sampling), and a mixed effect shows both pickers.

Steps:

- Dashboard + ModeDeviceScreen: derive sections from that. The Video/Audio toggle stays as the switcher for now.

Today's UX must look the same; this is a refactor.

title: Node prep 9 (spike): run video and audio capture at the same time on each platform
description:
Pipeline::build picks one input ('Video wins if both could apply'). Mixing screen and audio in one graph is the graph's main new capability, and it assumes both captures run together. Prove that before graph code.

Spike, throwaway or behind a dev flag: build both inputs and both orchestrators in one Pipeline and tick both. Check per platform:
- Mac: ScreenCaptureKit stream + process tap together (TCC prompts, the -3801 history in docs/lessons/input.md, CPU after Aurora-3qh).
- Linux: screencast portal + PipeWire audio stream together (one PipeWire runtime/thread or two; portal session).
- Windows: DXGI/WGC capture + miniaudio loopback together.
Measure CPU and tick timing for both vs each alone. Note which output wins when both send (expected: pick one Frame, or mix in a later graph node).

Not in scope: UI, config shape, the mixing itself.
acceptance_criteria: Per-platform result logged in docs/log (works / blocked + why), with CPU numbers; lessons filed for any capture conflict; NodeGraphPipeline.md updated with the outcome.
notes:
Also (2026-10-01): Mac needs Screen Recording + audio permission at once; the setup flow never asks for both today. Needs time on all three machines.
After Aurora-9ig: Pipeline (core/Runtime/src/Pipeline.cpp) holds either a video or an audio orchestrator via m_isAudioMode; running both at once changes that one class, not three main.cpp copies.

title: Node prep 7: apply Tuning edits to the running pipeline without a full reload
description:
Every PUT /api/config calls onConfigChanged -> PipelineHost::reload(), which rebuilds the whole Pipeline, including output init (Hue DTLS handshake, 1-3s). TuningFields.js's header documents working around this with gesture-end commits. NodeGraphPipeline.md's UX section assumes param edits go straight to the live node.

Classify fields by what a change needs:
- Hot (processing only): the 11 audio* AudioEffectSettings fields, transitionSmoothing, interpolation. Needs AudioOrchestrator::setSettings and an Orchestrator config/settings setter, applied under PipelineHost's lock.
- Probably hot, verify: refreshRate (tick interval only, in PipelineHost) and subsampleWidth (setCaptureWidthHint + rescale; check the Mac SCK hint does not restart the stream).
- Structural, keep reload: activeInputName/activeAudioInputName, activeOutputNames, activeMonitorName, audioTargetSinkName, port/bind IP.
SettingsRoutes PUT compares old vs new config and calls a hot-apply callback when only hot fields changed, else reload. Fields come from ParamSchema/descriptors (Aurora-ta5) so the hot list isn't hand-kept in two places.

Open (not decided): whether sliders then PUT while dragging (throttled) instead of on release.
acceptance_criteria: Changing any hot field via PUT /api/config changes output within one tick with no output re-init (no DTLS handshake in logs); structural fields still reload; config.json persists the same as today; tests cover the classification.
notes:
Watch (2026-10-01): PUT /api/config loads/saves config.json outside PipelineHost's lock, and Pipeline::build also saves derived refreshRate/subsampleWidth. Hot-apply needs one owner for config writes. Hot work adds to the lock Aurora-cgr is about. May make Aurora-vf1.2/vf1.4 unnecessary; revisit them after.
After Aurora-9ig (2026-10-01): the reload path is one function in core, Aurora::Runtime::reloadPipelineFromDisk (core/Runtime/src/Pipeline.cpp), used by the settings PUT, Hue pairing and POST /api/reload. Hot-apply goes there (or a PipelineHost method next to reload()), under PipelineHost's lock; one change covers all three apps. AuroraPipelineTests is the place for its tests.

title: Node prep 6: move Pipeline/PipelineHost from the three main.cpp files into core/Runtime
description:
Pipeline + PipelineHost are copied in app/linux, app/mac and app/windows main.cpp (~250 lines each; Mac's comment says 'ported unchanged from app/linux'). Node prep 7-9 all change this code, so each would land three times. Move the shared part into core/Runtime and leave per-platform hooks in the apps: input-name dispatch, Mac audioPermissionLikelyDenied, Linux sink/status routes, ScopedPhaseTimer.

Found 2026-10-01 while scoping hot tuning, capability-driven Dashboard and the dual-capture spike.
design: core/Runtime must not link platform Input libs. Apps inject platform pieces via a factory/callback interface (input construction incl. default input name). Platform hooks to keep out of core: input-name dispatch and default name (linux='linux', mac='dummy', windows='windows'); log sink (Windows logLine vs std::cout/cerr on Linux/Mac); reload error mapping (Mac catches Input::Mac::PermissionError -> 'permission_denied:'/'permission_pending:'); no-audio-build error text (differs per platform); Mac audioPermissionLikelyDenied and Linux audioSinkStatus (both dynamic_cast to platform grabbers); ScopedPhaseTimer output. Audio guards: Windows has no AURORA_RUNTIME_AUDIO_AVAILABLE ifdefs, Linux/Mac do; the shared code needs one consistent guard scheme.
acceptance_criteria: One Pipeline/PipelineHost in core/Runtime used by all three apps; app main.cpp files keep only platform hooks. Also in core/Runtime, replacing the three identical app copies: Registry; registerMonitorsRoute (GET /api/monitors); registerReloadRoute (POST /api/reload); and one shared 'load fresh Config -> PipelineHost::reload -> return error' function that the reload route, the registerSettingsRoutes callback and the registerPairingRoutes callback all call. Pairing's extra registerOutputs step stays app-side. New core tests for Pipeline/PipelineHost (build, reload, video vs audio mode, listZones/updateZone) and the two routes, written and passing against current behavior BEFORE the move, still green after. Existing Parity tests only cover Orchestrator/AudioOrchestrator, not Pipeline, so they alone don't prove no-change. Core ctest (new tests + Parity) green on Linux, Windows, Mac; app builds on each.

Change A (embed + serving):
1. embed_webroot.py: split any file over ~60 KB into pieces joined at static init, so a possible MSVC total-length limit (C1091) no longer matters. Keep \xNN isolation and explicit lengths. Escape '?' to silence GCC's trigraph warning. Add a namespace argument for a second map. 2. Server: add serveEmbeddedFilesAt(prefix, map); existing serveEmbeddedFiles callers stay unchanged. It works alongside the dev static mount; a trailing-slash path serves index.html; the bare prefix redirects to prefix/. Add contentTypeFor entries for .mjs, .map, .woff2, .wasm, .webp and .md. Change B (editor build):
3. web/graph-editor/: exact-pinned package.json, committed lockfile, engines node >=22.12 (Node 20 reached end of life 2026-04), .npmrc with ignore-scripts=true and engine-strict=true, vite base '/graph-editor/' with asset URLs built from import.meta.env.BASE_URL, build.license writing THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, dev server proxying /api to Aurora for hot reload, .gitignore for node_modules and dist.
4. CMake module: root option AURORA_ENABLE_GRAPH_EDITOR, OFF by default. find_program(NAMES npm.cmd npm), fatal with a pointer to Building.md only when the option is ON. Custom commands: plain 'npm ci' (no hardcoded network/cache flags, so npm_config_* env vars still apply for offline builds), stamped on package-lock.json; 'npm run build -- --outDir <bindir> --emptyOutDir', stamped on a source glob; embed DEPENDS on the build stamp. AURORA_GRAPH_EDITOR_DIST=<dir> skips npm entirely.
5. Apps: when ON, serve the editor map under /graph-editor/ in dev and standalone modes alike. install() the notice on Linux and Windows; copy it into Licenses/ on Mac.
6. linux.yml/windows.yml: setup-node 22 plus the option (ready for when Aurora-lzw unblocks CI). Building.md: Node >=22.12 and the option. FutureSteamOSSupport.md: one line saying the editor build is offline-ready (Flatpak node generator, AUR npm cache), relying on the committed lockfile, exact pins, no install scripts, plain npm ci and the prebuilt-bundle setting.
7. Verify by hand on Linux, Windows (MSVC) and Mac, logged: /graph-editor/ loads; with the option OFF the embedded header is unchanged and no Node is needed; touching a C++ file doesn't rerun vite.

Isolation: the npm build sits behind a CMake option that is off by default (e.g. AURORA_BUILD_GRAPH_EDITOR); with it off, the app builds need no Node and produce the same embedded webroot as before; editor sources and node_modules live in web/graph-editor/, and the bundle is written to the build dir, never under web/ui/ (aurora_embed_webroot collects every file under web/ui).

Investigation 2026-10-01 (Linux, scratchpad spike: Vite 8.3.2, React 19.3, @xyflow/react 12.12):
- Bundle: one JS file of 399 KB (126 KB gzip) + 17 KB CSS. That is about 6x MSVC's believed ~64 KB limit on a concatenated literal (C1091, still unverified; the largest file embedded today is 40 KB). The current embed_webroot.py output (16000-char pieces) compiles and round-trips byte-identical on GCC (1.0s, 92 MB). MSVC still needs checking on Windows.
- Minified JS contains '??!'. Trigraphs are gone in C++20 (all apps use cxx_std_20), so nothing is corrupted, but GCC warns (-Wtrigraphs). Escaping '?' as '\?' in the encoder silences it.
- Vite 8 has build.license built in: it emits a markdown notice for all 17 bundled packages (MIT/ISC/BSD-3, all GPL-compatible). No rollup-plugin-license needed.
- Vite 8 needs Node ^20.19 || >=22.12. Linux box has 24.14; web.yml pins 22.

The embedded catch-all maps '' to index.html only at the root ('graph-editor/' would 404). A bare /graph-editor needs a redirect to the trailing-slash path.
- Build: Vite outputs hashed filenames at build time, so aurora_embed_webroot's configure-time glob can't track them. Depend on a vite-build stamp instead. embed_webroot.py hardcodes namespace Aurora::EmbeddedWebRoot, so it needs a namespace argument for a second map.

- Dev loop pattern: RockyRoad proxies its API through the Vite dev server. For the editor, 'npm run dev' with server.proxy for /api to the running Aurora port gives hot reload without rebuilding C++.

Caveat from RockyRoadImport: patch-package runs as postinstall, so if the editor ever needs a patched dependency, run it explicitly after npm ci.
- RockyRoad uses caret ranges, and its two projects drifted onto different Vite majors (7 vs 8). Pin exact versions in package.json; the lockfile is the real pin for npm ci.

title: Audio tuning fields can drive NaN/Inf into Color::fromHSV's uint8_t cast (UB)
description:
PUT /api/config {"audioCentroidRangeHz": 0} (or any value that zeroes the denominator) reaches Processing::AudioProcessing::updateDrift's centroidDelta / settings.centroidRangeHz divide (core/AudioProcessing/src/AudioProcessing.cpp) with no zero-guard -- Config::setAudioCentroidRangeHz (core/Runtime/src/Config.cpp:167) has no clamp, unlike setTransitionSmoothing's std::clamp(..., 0.f, 0.97f) a few lines above it. The resulting NaN/Inf survives wrapDegrees's fmod and reaches Color::fromHSV (core/Contracts/include/Aurora/Contracts/Color.hpp:103-126): every 'hPrime < N' branch compares false against NaN, falling through to the last else, and static_cast<ChannelDepth>(std::round(NaN)) at the return is undefined behavior -- inside fromHSV itself, before the value ever reaches Smoother. Reachable today via the real REST API (a slider drag to 0 or a typo'd PUT), not hypothetical, and not specific to the node-graph work discussed in docs/planning/NodeGraphPipeline.md (though that work will add more reachable paths to the same class of bug).

## Context
Found while reviewing docs/planning/NodeGraphPipeline.md's live-preview fail-state section (Aurora-planning conversation, 2026-09-30) -- flagged there as a Smoother risk, corrected on closer read to be Color::fromHSV's own cast that fires first.
acceptance_criteria: audioCentroidRangeHz (and any other audio* tuning field used as a divisor: currently just this one, confirmed by reading updateDrift/updateBounce in full) is clamped away from zero in its Config setter, matching setTransitionSmoothing's pattern. Color::fromHSV gets a non-finite guard at its cast site as defense in depth (covers future callers, e.g. the node-graph work, not just this one path). Test: PUT audioCentroidRangeHz=0 in audio mode with a real onset, confirm no UB/crash and a sane color out, plus a unit test asserting fromHSV(NaN, ...) returns a defined Color rather than invoking UB.
close_reason: Fixed: setAudioCentroidRangeHz clamps to [100,8000] (NaN->default), fromHSV guards non-finite to black + clamps channels pre-cast. Tests in RuntimeTests/AudioProcessingTests pass; full core ctest 75/75.

title: AGENTS.md never points to docs/README.md's Id:/[[id]] convention; 5 dead docs/BrowserAnalysis.md citers outside check-links.sh scope
description:
Audited 2026-09-29 in response to: "Is the AGENTS.md to docs README logic
robust enough a new agent won't start pathing rather than make a link for
new docs?" Answer: no, confirmed by both a structural gap and live dead
links.

Structural gap: AGENTS.md's "Where things go" section -- the entry point an
agent reads before filing/citing a doc -- never mentions the Id:/[[id]]
convention or links to docs/README.md at all. The only README.md it points
to is docs/lessons/README.md, for a different topic (lessons filing). An
agent that only reads AGENTS.md has no way to discover the convention
exists and will default to bare relative-path citations for any new doc.

Live evidence: AGENTS.md line 13 itself cites `docs/BrowserAnalysis.md`,
which no longer exists -- the file moved to docs/archive/BrowserAnalysis.md
(Id: browser-analysis) during Aurora-w4c. Not just stale, dead, and it
models the wrong citation style for the next agent to copy. Same dead path
also found in:
- web-processing/README.md:7
- web/demo/README.md:14
- web/demo/CLAUDE.md:16
- web/demo/AGENTS.md:5

None of these were caught by check-links.sh (scans only docs/ and
.claude/skills/) or by Aurora-w4c's migration pass -- w4c was scoped to
docs/ only and skipped the repo-wide external-citer grep sweep that
Aurora-d8g's ImplementationPlan.md pass did do. Real inconsistency between
the two migrations, and exactly the lesson already on file in
docs/lessons/architecture-process.md ("A citer outside docs/'s scan scope
can go dead on a doc move and nothing catches it").

Two fixes:
1. Fix the 5 dead docs/BrowserAnalysis.md citations -> [[browser-analysis]]
   (or [[browser-analysis#anchor]] where line-anchored).
2. Add a line to AGENTS.md's "Where things go" pointing at docs/README.md's
   "Citing other docs" convention, the same way it already points at
   docs/lessons/README.md for lessons -- so a new agent filing a new doc
   actually finds the rule instead of pattern-matching off a stale example.

Verify with check-links.sh + check-lessons.sh after.

title: Mac: second launch doesn't reopen the browser (LaunchServices intercepts before InstanceLock runs)
description: Real regression, not a technicality: found while investigating Aurora-qps.4. GUILaunchUX.md's decided design ('second launch opens the configured URL and exits') assumes a second open/double-click always spawns a second process that runs InstanceLock, finds the lock held, and calls openWebBrowser(url) before exiting -- true on Windows/Linux, which have no OS-level single-instance-per-bundle behavior of their own. macOS does: LaunchServices recognizes the bundle identifier is already running and never spawns a second process at all, confirmed directly ('open --stdout/--stderr' on a second launch got refused with "Application ... was already running", and ps showed only the original process ever existed). Under LSUIElement agent mode (Aurora-qps.3, no Dock icon), this means a second double-click today does nothing visible at all -- no browser tab, no window, nothing. See docs/MacSupport.md, 'LaunchServices intercepts a second launch before InstanceLock ever runs' for the full investigation.
acceptance_criteria: Implement an NSApplicationDelegate (wired up alongside TrayIcon's existing [NSApplication sharedApplication] bootstrap in TrayIcon.mm) that handles a reopen -- applicationShouldHandleReopen:hasVisibleWindows: and/or listening for the kAEReopenApplication Apple Event directly, since accessory apps have no windows for the former to reliably key off -- and calls openWebBrowser(url) itself. Test: with Aurora already running (tray up, Dock hidden), open/double-click Aurora.app again and confirm a browser tab actually opens to the configured URL this time.
close_reason: Root cause found via a throwaway probe before touching real code: TrayIcon::pump()'s bare CFRunLoopRunInMode (Aurora-qps.2) was enough for NSStatusItem clicks but never delivers Apple Events -- LaunchServices' reopen event routes through -sendEvent:, which CFRunLoopRunInMode never calls. Isolated empirically: built two minimal probe bundles testing both applicationShouldHandleReopen: (delegate) and a raw NSAppleEventManager registration, as both accessory and regular (Dock-visible) apps -- neither handler style fired under the old pump regardless of accessory status, ruling out an LSUIElement-specific suppression. Switching the probe's pump to -nextEventMatchingMask:/-sendEvent: (NSDefaultRunLoopMode, same safe mode as before -- never common modes, tao-apps/tao#1324 still holds) made the standard delegate method fire reliably, so no need for the lower-level raw registration after all. Implemented for real: TrayIcon.mm gains AuroraTrayAppDelegate (applicationShouldHandleReopen:, calls the same onLaunch callback Launch UI's menu item already uses) set as NSApp.delegate, and pump() switched to the verified nextEventMatchingMask/sendEvent: drain. Verified end to end on real hardware: WebUI/tray/Dock-hidden all still correct after rebuild, a second 'open' while Aurora was already running opened/focused a browser tab (user confirmed), and the tray's own Launch UI/Stop menu items still dispatch correctly under the new pump (user confirmed, re-testing for a regression since the pump mechanism itself changed) -- process exited cleanly on Stop.

title: Mac: LaunchServices single-instance semantics vs InstanceLock
description: Newly surfaced open, not covered by GUILaunchUX.md or MacSupport.md: Windows and Linux both rely entirely on Aurora's own InstanceLock + 'second launch opens the configured URL and exits' logic for double-click dedup -- there is no OS-level app-instance dedup underneath them. macOS is different: LaunchServices itself tracks whether a bundle identifier is already running and may re-activate the existing process instead of spawning a second one at all, before Aurora's own main() ever runs -- especially once LSUIElement/agent mode is active and there's no visible window to activate to. This could make InstanceLock's second-launch handoff partially dead code on Mac, or could interact with it in an unconsidered way.
acceptance_criteria: With Aurora already running (tray up, Dock hidden per Aurora-qps.3), double-click Aurora.app again from Finder. Check via ps whether a second aurora-app-mac process actually launches, or whether LaunchServices no-ops/re-activates the first one instead. Confirm the configured URL still opens either way. Write the finding back into docs/MacSupport.md next to the existing second-launch design (GUILaunchUX.md's 'second launch opens the configured URL and exits' decision).
close_reason: Confirmed directly on real hardware, no GUI/mouse simulation needed ('open <bundle>' invokes the identical LaunchServices path a Finder double-click does). Launched Aurora once, then launched it again while the first instance was still running, using 'open --stdout/--stderr' to redirect the second launch's streams so its behavior would be observable even if it exited fast. open itself refused, printing 'Application ... was already running and so the redirected stdin/stdout/stderr provided could not be set' -- and ps confirmed only the original process ever existed, not a second one that ran InstanceLock's not-held branch and exited quickly. LaunchServices intercepts entirely: main()/InstanceLock/openWebBrowser(url) never execute on a second launch. Real consequence under LSUIElement (qps.3): a second double-click today does nothing visible at all. Finding written into docs/MacSupport.md next to GUILaunchUX.md's second-launch design. Follow-up fix filed as Aurora-qps.7 (NSApplicationDelegate reopen handling) rather than folded into this investigation -- real AppKit plumbing, not a one-line change.

title: Mac: wire TrayIcon into app/mac (NSStatusItem + menu + tick-loop pump)
description: New Objective-C++ source (input/mac's ScreenCaptureKitGrabber.mm PIMPL pattern is the precedent for keeping AppKit types out of the C++ side), constructed after InstanceLock succeeds. Same onLaunch/onStop callback shape as app/linux's TrayIcon for interface consistency -- but deliberately NOT its worker-thread + std::promise/future pattern. NSStatusItem must live on the main thread, which app/mac's tick loop already owns (unlike Linux, which needs a separate thread for its GMainLoop), so Mac's tray sidesteps the whole class of bug Aurora-nzd hit on Linux (promise moved into the worker thread, dtor later called get_future() on the moved-from object -- std::terminate on every shutdown). The tick loop's bare sleep_until gets the CFRunLoopRunInMode(kCFRunLoopDefaultMode, ...) pump added alongside it, mirroring Windows' PeekMessage/DispatchMessage pump at app/windows/src/main.cpp:1176-1181.
acceptance_criteria: Real aurora-app-mac build via the mac-app preset. Tray icon renders; Launch UI opens the actual running WebUI; Stop calls pipelineHost.shutdown() and exits cleanly. Cross-check tick cadence at a high refresh-rate setting against Aurora-cgr (tick loop can starve the API mutex) -- confirm the added per-tick pump call doesn't measurably worsen that.

New app/mac/src/TrayIcon.mm (PIMPL, matching ScreenCaptureKitGrabber.mm's pattern) + app/mac/include/Aurora/App/TrayIcon.hpp wired into AuroraApp; CMakeLists.txt gets enable_language(OBJCXX), AppKit link, and a make_tray_icon.sh custom command (18px/36px PNGs from the same 1024px master make_icns.sh already uses -- ships full-color, isTemplate=YES discards RGB at load time, per the qps.1-adjacent preview investigation). main.cpp constructs TrayIcon right after webUiBound/url are known (Linux's exact placement) and calls trayIcon.pump() once per tick-loop iteration after the sleep_until, scoped to kCFRunLoopDefaultMode only. Built clean via the mac-app preset, launched the real bundle with 'open' (not a direct exec, matching the actual user launch path) against a --fresh config root, confirmed the WebUI bound (curl'd /api/version). User confirmed live: the Aurora 'A' mark rendered in the menu bar, Launch UI opened the WebUI, Stop quit the app -- process exited cleanly (no crash, no hang) confirmed via ps. Not exercised: the Aurora-cgr high-refresh-rate tick-cadence cross-check -- this run had no configured pipeline (dummy input, no outputs), so tick timing under real load wasn't stressed; worth a follow-up look if cgr work ever touches the same loop. Clears the way for qps.3 (LSUIElement agent mode).

title: Mac: manual click-test of NSStatusItem run-loop-pump probe

title: Mac: stream health on lock/display sleep (isHealthy() decision)
description: IVideoInput has no error/health signaling hook today -- grabFrameSubsample just returns whatever's buffered. macOS suspends capture on screen lock far more aggressively than Linux/Windows privacy suspension. Decide whether to add an optional isHealthy() (default true, so Linux/Windows are unaffected) based on what's actually observed when locking mid-stream, not what's assumed. (docs/MacSupport.md#build-sequencing, phase 7).
acceptance_criteria: Lock the screen mid-stream; document whether the app crashes, freezes, silently serves a stale frame, or can report unhealthy; ship whichever contract change (if any) the observed behavior calls for.
close_reason: Observed live: locking mid-stream does NOT freeze or crash the app -- SCStream keeps calling back with frames tagged SCFrameStatusIdle (not .complete), and only after an extended lock (over a minute, exact threshold unconfirmed) does macOS tear the stream down entirely, firing didStopWithError with a real NSError ('Failed to find any displays or windows to capture'). Before this fix, nothing reacted to that: m_impl->stream/output kept pointing at the dead objects, so _ensureStream() (Aurora-8mk.6's lazy-rebuild path) thought capture was still fine and never attempted a rebuild -- grabFrameSubsample() would have silently served one frozen frame forever with zero signal. Fix: added IVideoInput::isHealthy() (default true, Linux/Windows unaffected), ScreenCaptureKitGrabber's didStopWithError: now clears stream/output/rebuildAttempted and sets healthy=false under the existing frameMutex (extended to guard this state too, since the delegate callback runs on its own dispatch queue independent of the app's own threads), and Orchestrator::update() skips a tick while unhealthy instead of re-pushing a stale frame. Recovery reuses Aurora-8mk.6's existing lazy-rebuild machinery unchanged -- no new reconnect subsystem needed. Verified live: didStopWithError fired cleanly under a real invocation (triggered via a pipeline-rebuild race during an activeMonitorName change) with no crash/hang and correct mutex-protected state clearing; configureAndStartStream() (the same function _ensureStream() calls to recover) succeeded dozens of times today across every relaunch. title: Tray icon sometimes missing: RegisterStatusNotifierItem races async bus-name acquisition
description: runTrayWorker calls g_bus_own_name (async, no callbacks) then immediately RegisterStatusNotifierItem. notes: Live diagnosis 2026-09-23 with Aurora running (PID 3907, fixed build): stderr showed 'bus name never acquired'. Live state matched exactly: name owned per busctl, watcher list missing Aurora. Fix: pump the context (g_main_context_iteration) each wait pass. Rebuilt clean, app/linux 65/65 green. description:

Must remain dual-mode:
- Double-click / Explorer launch: no console window at all.
- Launched from an existing console (cmd / PowerShell / Windows Terminal): attach back to the parent console via AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) + reopen CONOUT$/CONERR$ so URL print, status, and fatals still appear there, and Ctrl+C still stops the app. Explicit --console flag (and/or AURORA_CONSOLE env) forces attach even when auto-detect is ambiguous.

Requires: rerouting all cout/cerr output (URL print, status, fatals) to a dual sink (attached console when present, otherwise a file log in the config root or equivalent), since headless early-fatals would otherwise look like 'double-click does nothing'; a message-box/event-log fallback for startup failures; tray Stop + /api/stop remain the only headless exits (flag already shared). Out of 1.0.2 by design (console is load-bearing for diagnostics until the tray is proven).

Acceptance: (1) Explorer double-click shows no console flash and leaves a tray icon; (2) `Aurora.exe` from cmd prints WebUI URL + status and Ctrl+C stops cleanly; (3) `Aurora.exe --console` from Run dialog / shortcut attaches visibly; (4) headless startup failure leaves log + message box, never silent exit.

Sink table for the 17 cout/cerr sites in app/windows/src/main.cpp (all resolved, no open questions):

1. Status chatter on stdout -> dual sink (attached console + log file), verbatim:

   - "Config root: ..." (882)
   - "WebUI: opening ..." first-setup branch (1033)
   - "Stopping..." (1069)

2. Degraded-but-running warnings on stderr -> log file always, console when
   attached, NEVER a message box (routine on fresh installs):
   - "Unknown output ..." (231)
   - "Pipeline not started ... WebUI still available" (931)
   - "[descriptors] collision ..." (953-956)
   - "Could not bind WebUI ..." (1041)
   - "No notification area ..." (776)

4. True fatal (catch-all "Fatal:" 1083) -> log + message box (+ console when

   Delete with its TEMP comment when the pairing repro closes.

Verified non-issues: no stdin reads anywhere in the slice (no cin/getline/
STD_INPUT_HANDLE), so detaching stdin is free. Tray tooltip/balloon snprintf
sites (773, 835-837) are not console output and are out of scope.

Resolutions for the four flagged opens (2026-09-23):

1. Log bootstrap (DECIDED): two-phase init. Buffer all sink output in memory
   from process start; flush to <configRoot>/aurora.log once configRoot is
   known. If configRoot itself is unresolvable, fall back to
   %TEMP%/Aurora/aurora.log. A Fatal before any file exists still boxes, and

2. Message-box scope (DECIDED): only the catch-all Fatal boxes. Degraded-
   but-running warnings (bind failure, pipeline-not-started, descriptor

   when console attached, "Tray Stop or /api/stop to stop." when headless.

title: [bug] Dashboard shows only logo, Stop, version -- no content
description:
Related to Aurora-a4l / Aurora-jep. On the dashboard, only the top-bar logo, the Stop button, and the version footer render; no controls, top tier, or accordion sections appear.

What the code says: DashboardScreen.mount (web/ui/screens/DashboardScreen.js) renders the top bar, then awaits _loadAll(). Logo + Stop + version are all painted inside _loadAll() BEFORE _loadZoneData() and _render() run -- so this exact skeleton means _loadAll() aborted after the version probe and before _render().

Prime suspect, verified by reading: _loadZoneData() awaits this.entertainmentConfigSelect.load() with NO try/catch (line ~192) -- every other fetch in _loadAll/_loadZoneData is guarded except this one. If that load rejects (bridge unreachable, entertainment config missing, non-JSON response), _loadAll() throws, _render() never runs, and the page is stuck at logo + Stop + version. Check the browser console for the rejection and the /api/hue/entertainment-configs (or equivalent) response.

Fix direction: wrap the entertainmentConfigSelect.load() call in try/catch like the neighboring fetches (degrade to empty picker + surfaced error), and/or add a mount-level catch that renders an error state instead of a silent skeleton.
notes:
Timing probe (serial, dashboard order): all 8 endpoints fast when warm -- capabilities/version/connection/config ~0.00s, monitors 0.07s, zones 0.04s, entertainment-configurations 0.13s, hue/channels 0.14s; wall total 0.44s. Verdict: no permanently slow endpoint. The earlier skeleton-then-load was cold-start cost (grabber init, bridge first contact) amplified by _loadAll awaiting everything serially before _render. Fix stays frontend: parallelize independent fetches / render progressively so cold start shows progress instead of a bare skeleton.
Cold-call anatomy (read from app/linux/src/main.cpp): Pipeline::build runs synchronously at boot BEFORE the server binds -- output->init (Hue bridge first contact), input->init (X11 RandR enumeration / PipeWire portal negotiation, can block seconds), orchestrator init. On first setup the browser auto-opens right after bind, and with no inputs configured yet build returns nullptr ('WebUI still available for setup'), so early UI fetches legitimately see empty monitors/zones. Worse, every settings PUT funnels into PipelineHost::reload, which rebuilds the pipeline -- so each NUX save re-pays full input re-init, not just boot. Candidate fixes: (1) frontend parallelize + progressive render + refetch-empty-monitors; (2) reload reuses the video input when selection unchanged; (3) bind-first/build-in-background with a readiness endpoint; (4) cache monitor list + bridge responses; (5) bound bridge timeouts.
Fix suggestions (complexity-estimated, see session 2026-09-20): [S1] Frontend parallelize + progressive render -- batch independent fetches with Promise.all, render sections as they arrive. Small-to-medium, JS only; mirror check needed in web/demo/vendor/webui + node web-processing tests. Do first. [S2] Reload reuses video input when selection unchanged -- only rebuild what the PUT altered. Medium C++ (linux+windows); breaks documented reconstruction-not-mutation invariant, watch orchestrator input references + shutdown(isReplacement). Highest-value backend fix. [S3] Bind-first, build-in-background + readiness endpoint. Medium-large; changes startup contract, both slices. Only if boot itself becomes the complaint. [S4] Bridge timeouts -- bound Hue HTTP client timeouts so a stale bridge IP degrades instead of stalling. Small.

title: [bug] Video monitor list empty on Linux while screen visibly feeds lights
description:
On Linux, the video monitor picker never populated, yet the screen was visibly feeding the lights -- capture itself works, only enumeration/display of monitors is broken.

Why this can happen (candidate causes, unconfirmed):
1. Stale fetch while in audio mode: GET /api/monitors returns only what the live pipeline constructed (PipelineHost::listMonitors returns empty when m_videoInput is null; ModeDeviceScreen.js notes it comes back empty in audio mode). If the UI fetched the list before video input existed and never refetched after capture started, the picker stays empty while lights feed fine.
2. Enumeration/capture split-brain on Linux: lights can be fed by the PipeWire path (or X11 fallback on a default monitor) while the monitor list comes from XRandR enumeration in X11Grabber::_initMonitorsList, which throws 'No monitor available' when no output is connected-with-crtc (Wayland/XWayland, disabled outputs). Capture works, list does not.
3. Timing: monitors fetched before the video input finished constructing; UI caches the empty result.
4. Wrong-instance: the grabber feeding lights is not the input instance answering monitors().

Next step to discriminate: on the affected box, capture the raw GET /api/monitors response, note which grabber (PipeWire vs X11) is active in the logs, and check for XRandR 'No monitor available' errors. That separates a backend enumeration failure (2) from a frontend stale-fetch problem (1/3).
notes:
Timing probe: GET /api/monitors now returns 200 with 102 bytes -- a populated list, not an empty array. Backend enumeration (XRandR/PipeWire) works fine on this box. This promotes the stale-fetch hypotheses (fetched while in audio mode / before video input construction, then never refetched) and demotes backend enumeration failure. Fix direction: UI should refetch monitors when video mode becomes active rather than trusting the first (possibly empty) result.
Fix suggestions: [S1] UI re-polls/refetches /api/monitors while empty and refetches when video mode becomes active, instead of trusting the first result. Small, JS only (part of the dashboard frontend fix). [S4] Monitor-list caching -- verify before building: if enumeration happens once in input->init and monitors() just returns the stored list (0.07s warm supports this), per-call caching buys nothing. Check where the per-call cost lives first.

title: Manifest-mode core build on Windows picks vcpkg httplib 0.58 over fetched 0.46: ODR segfault in AuroraPipelineTests
description: Found 2026-10-01 validating Aurora-9ig on Windows. A core standalone configure with the vcpkg toolchain and manifest mode ON (build/core-test) installs cpp-httplib 0.58.0 into vcpkg_installed. find_package(httplib 0.46) there reports httplib_DIR-NOTFOUND, so core fetches 0.46.0 as well. AuroraPipelineTests' include path lists vcpkg_installed/.../include before _deps/httplib-src, while AuroraNetwork lists httplib-src first, so the test TU and HttpServer.cpp compile different httplib versions (ODR). Test 'Monitors and reload routes answer from PipelineHost' segfaults in httplib::Server::process_request on its first request, with any handler. AuroraNetworkTests escapes it only by include order. CI is unaffected (VCPKG_MANIFEST_MODE=OFF). Fix options: make find_package(httplib) accept the manifest copy (httplib_DIR/config), or pin one version and make both targets see the same header first (e.g. BEFORE include dirs on the httplib target, or drop cpp-httplib from core/vcpkg.json). Log: docs/log/2026-10-01-9ig-pipeline-to-core.md
acceptance_criteria: core standalone configured WITH manifest mode on Windows passes AuroraPipelineTests (121/121); one httplib version visible to every target in that configure
notes:
Analysis 2026-10-01. Root cause chain: core/vcpkg.json lists cpp-httplib -> manifest mode installs 0.58.0 in build/core-test/vcpkg_installed. core/CMakeLists.txt find_package(httplib 0.46 QUIET) REJECTS it: cpp-httplib's httplibConfigVersion.cmake only accepts a matching minor version (reproduced in a throwaway project: 'version found is not compatible'), so >=0.46 does not hold for 0.58. Core therefore also FetchContent-fetches 0.46.0 into _deps/httplib-src. Two copies reach include paths; order differs per target (AuroraNetwork: httplib-src first; AuroraPipelineTests: vcpkg_installed first, via OpenCV/Catch2/glm imported-target include dirs). Recommended fix: drop cpp-httplib from core/vcpkg.json (core already owns the fetch; one line). Alternatives rejected: bump pin to 0.58 (changes httplib for HA/Hue work needing 0.46 ws client); reorder include dirs (fragile, OpenCV include path still pulls the other copy). Also update docs/lessons/build-toolchain.md manifest-mode entry (names cpp-httplib in the manifest list) and the new httplib ODR entry.
Other-platform / other-dep check: (1) Linux CI: apt installs cmake ninja X11/pipewire/glib/aubio/opencv/curl/mbedtls dev packages, no httplib, no vcpkg -> fetched 0.46 only, same for Mac CI (brew cmake opencv curl aubio mbedtls pkg-config). Neither uses manifest mode. No issue in CI. (2) Local Linux/Mac with a distro/brew httplib: find_package would reject it (too old or minor mismatch) and the fetched copy is used; the system copy sits in /usr/include or /opt/homebrew/include, searched after -I dirs, so low risk; only a dep adding -I for that exact dir ahead of httplib-src could reproduce it. Not verified on a real Mac/Linux box. (3) Same manifest class for the other manifest deps: glm, Catch2, opencv4 are found from vcpkg_installed (glm_DIR/Catch2_DIR/OpenCV_DIR point there, nothing extra fetched), so a single copy each; nlohmann_json is fetched and not in the manifest. httplib is the only duplicate. (4) Windows app preset (no manifest, classic C:/vcpkg): no httplib installed there; CI installs only curl mbedtls aubio miniaudio; a dev who classic-installs cpp-httplib gets its include dir listed after httplib-src in the vcxproj, so fetched copy wins. (5) Only core/vcpkg.json exists. (6) httplib users: core/Network, core tests (Network, WebSocketSmoke, Pipeline), output/hue/tests/PairingRoutesTests; only core tests built with manifest on were affected. Fix NOT yet applied or verified (needs a manifest-mode reconfigure of core and a 121/121 run).

title: Fake HA: match real refresh-token behavior (no rotation, revoke, invalidation)
description:
tools/fake-home-assistant diverges from HA core f66cbe4 in ways that would mislead 4zr.2/4zr.5 (found in the 2dz review, facts in [[home-assistant-output]] 'Refresh-token lifecycle'):
- Rotates the refresh token on every refresh grant (fake_ha.py:322). Real HA returns only access_token/token_type/expires_in (components/auth/__init__.py:464). Code built on the fake could overwrite the store with an empty token against real HA.
- Wrong client_id on refresh returns invalid_grant; real returns invalid_request (:438). invalid_grant is reserved for unknown/expired tokens, which is the 'log in again' signal.
- No /auth/revoke (real: form field token, no auth, always 200; :237).
- No way to invalidate issued tokens (simulates 90-day expiry or revocation in HA's UI).
acceptance_criteria:
- Refresh grant returns no refresh_token; the same refresh token keeps working.

title: HA prep 7: OS secret store (Keychain / DPAPI / libsecret) behind one interface
description: An HA refresh token controls the whole home, so it must not sit in a JSON file. Hue's username/clientkey are plain JSON today (output/hue/src/CredentialsStore.cpp); moving them is optional. One core interface (get/set/delete by key), one implementation per platform. libsecret on Linux is a new dependency; check it's present on Ubuntu desktop and decide the fallback when no keyring is running. See [[home-assistant-output]].
acceptance_criteria:
- Fake (in-memory) backend unit tests on all three platforms; opt-in real-backend store/read/delete round-trip on Linux, Mac, Windows.
- Keys namespaced by config root: --fresh, AURORA_CONFIG_DIR roots and tests never see the real user's secrets.
- HA record = {haUrl, clientId, refreshToken} (or {haUrl, longLivedToken}); read with a different haUrl returns absent (enforces the 5i3 URL-change rule by construction).
- Threading contract written down: backend calls may block (keyring unlock prompt); only at connect/login/reset, never on the tick thread or under the API mutex.
- Decisions recorded in [[home-assistant-output]]: Mac signing vs Keychain ACL; Linux no-keyring cases (locked/autologin, no Secret Service, Flatpak portal); Windows Credential Manager vs DPAPI+file; Hue stays in JSON (recommended).
- Reset/disconnect deletes the OS entry, after POST /auth/revoke to HA.
notes:
Review 2026-10-02 (pre-build gaps):
- Mac: app/mac/CMakeLists.txt signs ad-hoc ('-') by default; Keychain ACLs bind to the code signature, so every rebuild or update prompts or fails. Needs a stable identity or an access group.
- Linux: the runtime libsecret-1.so.0 is present on Ubuntu desktop; libsecret-1-dev is not. Gate it behind a CMake option; linux.yml needs the headers; the CI real-backend test needs dbus-run-session plus an unlocked gnome-keyring-daemon.
- Windows: DPAPI only encrypts (still a file); Credential Manager (CredWrite/CredRead) is a real store and matches get/set/delete.
- Secret values never go in logs or error strings (test-pulse returns e.what()).
HA facts that shape the store (detail and line refs: [[home-assistant-output]] 'Refresh-token lifecycle'):
- The refresh token is never rotated: written once at login, read at connect. Low write rate, so blocking calls are fine there.
- The record must hold clientId (bound at login) and haUrl. A long-lived token is a separate shape.
- Values are small (refresh token 128 hex chars, long-lived JWT a few hundred bytes), well under Credential Manager's 2560-byte blob limit.
- Delete must be cheap and idempotent; the callers in 4zr.2 and 4zr.5 run it after revoke or on invalid_grant.

- core/Secrets (AuroraSecrets) built: ISecretStore, MemorySecretStore, scopeForConfigRoot, setBound/getBound, backends for libsecret, Keychain and Credential Manager, plus a no-libsecret stub. Decisions are in the HA doc's 'Secret store' section.

- Lesson candidates: weakly_canonical('root/.') keeps a trailing slash; unsetting DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS doesn't remove the bus (GIO falls back to XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus), so use unix:path=/nonexistent.
2026-10-02: fallback decided: session-only by default, opt-in FileSecretStore (owner-only, temp-then-rename; refuses to overwrite a corrupt file). Added the [real-write]/[real-read]/[real-cleanup] cross-binary pair. Linux: write, then a separate run reads Ok, then cleanup; no leftovers. Suite 54/54, core ctest 105/105. Remaining: Mac (rebuild prompt via the pair) and Windows compile + [real].
Mac 2026-10-02: core builds on Mac (Keychain backend), ctest 127/127, [real] 12/12. Rebuild pair with ad-hoc signing: [real-read] after a rebuild shows a system dialog for the login keychain password (Mac account password); Allow -> Ok; cleanup no prompt. Remaining: Deny -> Unavailable check; identity-signed run (expect no prompt); Windows compile + [real]; define returning-user Unavailable UX (token exists but unreadable: Deny, locked keychain, blank-password/auto-login) for 4zr.2/4zr.5. Details in docs/log/2026-10-02-2dz-secret-store.md.

Impact: delete after an app update (disconnect / invalid_grant cleanup in 4zr.2/4zr.5) may fail on Mac. From qy5.1: Homebrew dylibs are linked from /opt/homebrew, not bundled. Scope must include bundling them into Contents/Frameworks, rewriting install names, and signing each inside-out; otherwise notarization fails and the app can't run on a machine without Homebrew.
2026-09-29 feasibility (prototype in scratchpad, not in repo):
OPTION 1 (bundle) IS FEASIBLE. Transitive closure of the mac binary = 29 dylibs from 17 Homebrew packages, ~40 MB in Contents/Frameworks (app ~46 MB). A 30-line script (copy, install_name_tool -id/-change to @rpath, add_rpath @executable_path/../Frameworks, codesign each) produced a bundle with zero /opt/homebrew references that launches and serves the WebUI. CAVEAT: with ad-hoc signing the hardened runtime still rejects even the bundled dylibs ('different Team IDs' -- ad-hoc has no Team ID). Library validation only passes once app + every dylib are signed with the SAME Developer ID Team ID. So the no-entitlement result is unproven until the cert exists; until then disable-library-validation is needed to test. Also: arm64 only (Homebrew is arm64 here).
Packages: aubio (+libsndfile, flac, libogg, libvorbis, opus, mpg123, lame), opencv (+openblas, tbb, gcc runtime, libomp), openssl@3, mbedtls@3, brotli, zstd.

Verify flac/gcc details before release; Homebrew metadata only, not a legal review.

It DID launch, but DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES showed it loaded all 29 libs from /opt/homebrew and 0 from the bundle: the binary's absolute rpath /opt/homebrew/lib is searched before @executable_path/../Frameworks, and several Homebrew dylibs carry absolute rpaths too. tools/mac/bundle-dylibs.sh (qy5.6) deletes every rpath and re-adds only the bundle-relative one; verified 28 loaded from Contents/Frameworks, 0 from Homebrew. title: Mac: tray context menu blocks the pipeline tick loop while open
description: Confirmed live on Mac (Aurora-qps.2/.7's TrayIcon), 2026-09-28: opening the tray menu and holding it open froze real light-viz-relay frame delivery for the entire time it was open (a timestamped SSE-log capture showed a clean multi-second gap in frame arrival exactly matching the window the menu was held open, resuming the instant it closed -- not a rendering artifact, genuine pipeline stall). Root cause: TrayIcon::pump() calls [NSApp sendEvent:event] for the menu's click, and NSMenu's tracking runs as a nested, blocking loop inside that call -- it doesn't return until the menu closes. Aurora's tick loop and the AppKit pump share one thread by design (deliberately, to avoid the worker-thread promise/future bug class Aurora-nzd hit on Linux), so pipelineHost.tick() can't run again until the menu is dismissed. Checked Windows and Linux directly in code rather than assuming: Windows shares the exact same bug -- TrayIcon::showMenu() (app/windows/src/main.cpp:850-875) calls the documented-blocking TrackPopupMenuEx synchronously from trayWndProc, itself invoked via DispatchMessageA inside the identical single tick loop (main.cpp:1173-1181) -- so a Windows user right-clicking the tray icon almost certainly freezes the pipeline the same way, just never observed/tested. Linux is structurally immune: app/linux/src/TrayIcon.cpp runs its GMainLoop on its own dedicated worker thread (TrayIcon.cpp:334, std::thread), fully separate from the main thread's tick loop -- menu tracking there never touches the thread pipelineHost.tick() runs on. Deliberately low priority: judged acceptable for now (a menu is only open briefly, and the capture/output pipeline resuming instantly on close is a mild glitch, not data loss or a crash) -- filed for whenever tray UX gets revisited, not urgent.
acceptance_criteria: Mac tray menu held open (5-8s) causes no gap in pipeline frame delivery: timestamped SSE gap capture (tools/light-viz-relay/traygap.py) shows max gap comparable to Windows (~0.06s). /api/stop, tray Stop and SIGINT with the menu open all exit cleanly (no hang). Tick cadence unchanged under App Nap / accessory mode. Tray Launch UI, Stop and Apple-Event reopen (qps.7) still work.
notes:
Windows half split out and fixed as Aurora-anw (tray moved to its own thread; Win32 window affinity is per-thread, so no tick-loop move needed). Mac still needs the tick loop moved off the main thread (AppKit requires main for the pump); design pass on PipelineHost lock / shutdown ordering first. Repro/measure with the timestamped SSE gap capture (see docs/log/2026-09-29-windows-tray-threading.md).
2026-09-30 design decision: worker-thread option chosen over a common-modes run-loop timer (TrayIcon.hpp forbids kCFRunLoopCommonModes -- tao#1324 breaks menu tracking; and main never calls [NSApp run]). Plan: main thread keeps AppKit pump (nextEventMatchingMask w/ short timeout, NSDefaultRunLoopMode) + TrayIcon; tick loop moves to an RAII-joined worker thread (try/catch inside); g_stopRequested -> std::atomic<bool>; main joins tick thread then pipelineHost.shutdown() (order unchanged). PipelineHost mutex already multi-thread safe (reload() runs on HTTP thread); SCStream uses its own dispatch queue; nothing but TrayIcon.mm needs main. Risks: /api/stop with menu open (main blocked in tracking -> need cancelTracking dispatched to main, cf. Windows WM_CANCELMODE); App Nap/timer coalescing on worker (QoS/activity assertion). Windows half already done in Aurora-anw.

description: Follow-up to Aurora-1z9's open question, answered by reading PipelineHost::reload (app/linux/src/main.cpp:578-590): the replacement pipeline is built BEFORE the swap mutex is taken, so two concurrent PUT /api/config or POST /api/reload requests genuinely construct two PipewireGrabbers on separate pool threads. title: Mac: free Personal Team signing spike (SMAppService feasibility)
description: Deliberately low priority and not blocking the rest of this sequence: neither Windows nor Linux ship launch-at-login today. So Mac doing SMAppService now would leapfrog both shipped platforms rather than catch up to them -- kept open only to resolve the signing question raised in the 2026-09-28 investigation, not because it's scoped for near-term work. Research found ad-hoc signing is genuinely unreliable for SMAppService (no stable designated requirement across rebuilds), but a completely free Apple ID 'Personal Team' in Xcode gets a real, stable, Team-ID-backed certificate -- per Apple DTS/TN3127 guidance, this is the documented fix for 'unstable code identity' problems (their example: Keychain re-auth prompts), and does not require the $99 Developer Program. The commonly-cited 7-day Personal Team provisioning-profile expiry looks like it doesn't apply here: macOS only needs a provisioning profile for *restricted* entitlements, and Aurora's mac target has none -- so the certificate's own ~1-year validity is likely what actually governs, same order of magnitude free or paid. Log out and back in (not just relaunch -- login items need an actual login event) to confirm Aurora actually starts. Check System Settings -> Login Items shows an accurate entry, watching for the .notFound-despite-registered status gotcha found in research.

title: OFF audio toggle is a no-op via superbuild (core/input already configured before app/linux FORCE-sets)
description: AURORA_APP_ENABLE_LINUX_AUDIO_INPUT=OFF does not actually disable audio in a superbuild/preset configure. Root CMakeLists.txt adds input/linux before app/linux; input/linux's FetchContent_MakeAvailable(AuroraCore) configures core with default AURORA_CORE_ENABLE_AUDIO=TRUE first, so app/linux's later FORCE to OFF lands after core's add_subdirectory(AudioProcessing) already ran (FetchContent dedups by name). Likewise the NOT TARGET guard on app/linux's input/linux block skips its AURORA_INPUT_LINUX_ENABLE_AUDIO FORCE-set entirely. Evidence from build/linux-app-noaudio configured with =OFF: cache still has AURORA_INPUT_LINUX_ENABLE_AUDIO=ON, and aurora-app-linux flags.make still carries -DAURORA_RUNTIME_AUDIO_AVAILABLE=1 -DAURORA_INPUT_LINUX_AUDIO_AVAILABLE=1. Found while verifying Aurora-y1q: the bead's OFF-build acceptance passes vacuously today. Fix options: hoist the FORCE-sets into the root superbuild before add_subdirectory(input/linux), or make app/linux's sets unconditional (not behind NOT TARGET) and tolerate reconfig.

title: Mac: diagnose persistent Screen Recording -3801 despite Settings toggle showing enabled
description: During live video<->audio handoff testing on Mac (following Aurora-9z4/Aurora-zx4), video mode kept failing with ScreenCaptureKitGrabber's permission_denied (SCStreamErrorDomain -3801, 'no shareable displays') even after tccutil reset ScreenCapture, multiple full quit+relaunch cycles, and the Settings toggle visibly showing Aurora enabled. Two hypotheses tested and ruled out: TCC rate-limiting from rapid repeated requests (disproven by a 20s idle wait + single clean request, still denied) and a concurrent-enumeration race (same test). A scoped tccutil reset ScreenCapture com.aurora.app confirmed a real, matching stale entry existed. Root fix: macOS shows two different Screen Recording consent dialogs -- one offering only Settings/Deny (doesn't grant anything itself), and one offering an inline Approve (grants immediately) -- and only a fresh cycle that produced the Approve-button variant actually resulted in a working grant, confirmed via /api/monitors returning the real display. Video<->audio mode handoff confirmed working end to end afterward.
close_reason: Root cause found and confirmed live: macOS shows two different Screen Recording consent dialogs (Settings/Deny-only vs. an inline Approve), and only the Approve variant actually grants anything -- a Settings-routed toggle can read 'enabled' without backing a working grant, which is why quit/relaunch cycling alone didn't recover it. Ruled out TCC rate-limiting and a concurrent-enumeration race first via live idle-wait retests. Fixed via a scoped tccutil reset + a fresh deliberate grant that happened to produce the Approve dialog; confirmed via /api/monitors returning the real display and a full video<->audio mode handoff in the WebUI. Lesson filed in docs/lessons/input.md, session logged at the end of docs/log/2026-09-28-mac-audio-webui-banner.md. No code changes -- diagnosis and documentation only.

title: Linux tray icon (SNI): agent-first, tray as enhancement
description: Linux counterpart to Aurora-x2o for a later release (not 1.0.2): background agent via XDG autostart + Background-portal registration as the guaranteed trunk; StatusNotifierItem icon + dbusmenu (Launch UI / Stop, tooltip) as the enhancement leaf on KDE, Ubuntu-GNOME, Mint, Xfce. Stock GNOME (Fedora/Debian/Arch) has no tray host -- there the portal Background-Apps entry (presence + kill only) plus the browser UI is the whole story. Handoff semantics shared with 52o/x2o: second launch opens the configured URL (browsableAddress + port) and exits, never a duplicate server; Stop signals only our own process, never kill-by-port. Tray must degrade to fully-trayless operation with zero loss of function. Depends on Aurora-52o.

title: Mac: Intel (x86_64) support is unverified; scripts assume the Apple-silicon Homebrew prefix
description: Decision 2026-09-30: Aurora's Mac support is Apple silicon only; Intel is not supported or promised. Apple's macOS 27 is Apple-silicon only and Intel Macs top out at macOS 26 (per third-party sources, not confirmed on Apple's site). Gaps found if this is ever revisited: tools/mac/bundle-dylibs.sh, bundle-licenses.sh and verify-bundle.sh hard-code /opt/homebrew (Intel Homebrew is /usr/local; derive from brew --prefix); Homebrew bottles are single-architecture, so a universal bundle needs both builds plus lipo, or separate per-arch zips; Aurora's own code has no NEON/SSE intrinsics or arch flags, so it should build for x86_64, but ScreenCaptureKit capture, process-tap audio and hardened runtime are untested on Intel. No Intel Mac is available to test.
acceptance_criteria: Builds and runs on a real Intel Mac on macOS 15/26 with capture and audio verified; scripts derive the Homebrew prefix; release artifact strategy (universal vs per-arch) decided.

title: Mac: lower-target dylib build for macOS 15/26 users with their own signing setup
description: The prebuilt/notarized Mac zip targets macOS 27 because Homebrew bottles carry minos 27 (Aurora-qy5.8, resolved by declaring a 27 floor). This follow-up is optional: document and script a way to build the dylib closure with a lower MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET (15, or the code's real floor 14.2) so Apple-silicon Macs staying on 15/26 can run a bundle. Options: build on a runner/VM running the oldest target OS (Homebrew bottles then carry that minos), or build the closure from source (e.g. vcpkg arm64-osx triplet with VCPKG_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET plus a binary cache). Not for Intel (separate work). Deferred: only revisit if someone reports they cannot run the 27 build. Contributors can already build from source on their own older Mac with no cert (Homebrew bottles match their OS); anyone wanting a bundle for others supplies their own Developer ID and notary profile via the existing name-based scripts. Choosing 15 vs 14.2 is a promise/test decision, not a runtime one: a lower minos also runs on newer macOS.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, repeatable way to produce a bundle where verify-bundle.sh reports no minos WARN at the chosen floor, tested on at least one Mac running that floor OS; docs addendum states the new prebuilt floor.

title: Scope: audio-device dropdown for Mac and Windows (Linux shipped in 1.0.4)
description:
Linux got an audio-device dropdown in 1.0.4 (Aurora-67y/apn, commit 307fa75; docs/log/2026-09-30-audio-sink-dropdown.md and 2026-09-30-sink-dropdown-fetch-rework.md). This bead is the scoping note for bringing it to Mac and Windows. Estimates are from reading code, not from building anything.

PRODUCT QUESTION FIRST: on Linux the dropdown mattered because PipeWire exposes many virtual sinks. Most Mac/Windows users have one default output. Decide whether "follows the default output" is enough before spending the time.

ALREADY PLATFORM-NEUTRAL: config field audioTargetSinkName (core/Runtime Config.hpp, ConfigStore, SettingsRoutes) and the settings route. The frontend DeviceField audio dropdown (web/ui/DeviceField.js: lazy load, refresh on open, unlisted-persisted value stays selected, failure fallback) is written but Linux-specific in three places: fetches /api/linux/audio-sinks; shown only when audioInputs includes 'linux-audio' (ModeDeviceScreen.js, DashboardScreen.js); descriptor tag input.sink lives in input/linux.

1) SHARED FRONTEND (small, ~0.5 day): make route + gate + descriptor tag platform-neutral (common /api/audio-devices or per-platform URL; capability-based gate). Mirror into web/demo/vendor/webui, demo-shim.js (shim must answer every route) and tests. Do once, not three times.

2) WINDOWS (small-medium, ~1 day): input/windows/src/AudioGrabber.cpp uses miniaudio loopback with pDeviceID=nullptr (default playback device). Enumerate with ma_context_get_devices, pass the chosen ID into the loopback config. Decide what to store (WASAPI endpoint ID is stable; names can duplicate) and what happens when the saved device is gone (Linux silently falls back to default; that was flagged as a surprise, Aurora-4xq). Needs a Windows machine to verify.

3) MAC (medium, riskiest, ~1-1.5 days): input/mac/src/MacAudioGrabber.mm taps ALL system audio (initStereoGlobalTapButExcludeProcesses) and sets the aggregate device main sub-device from the default output UID, read once at init. Selecting a device means enumerating output devices via Core Audio (UID + name) and building a device-specific tap (verify the exact CATapDescription initializer in the SDK, macOS 14.2+ API). Semantics change from "everything the Mac plays" to "audio routed to that device". Non-default-device tap + aggregate is UNPROVEN here; needs a second output device (AirPods, USB DAC) to test. Existing gap: default-output changes are not followed today (read once at init); a dropdown makes that more visible.

Suggested order: shared frontend, Windows, Mac. Total ~2-3 days.
notes:
2026-10-01 discussion. NO DESIGN DECISION MADE; options only.

Today's default per platform (no setting):
- Linux: default sink, resolved by name once at start (AudioGrabber.cpp ~L311); does not follow later default-sink changes. Dropdown already lists every sink (AudioSinkList.cpp) but stores ONE name in audioTargetSinkName.
- Windows: default playback device loopback (pDeviceID=nullptr). Probably follows default changes via miniaudio WASAPI auto stream routing -- unverified.
- Mac: global process tap = everything every app plays, any device. Default output UID (read once at init) only sets the aggregate's clock sub-device.

Dropdown with today's default as first option:
- Linux: shipped (Default + sinks, single pick).
- Windows: Default + playback devices; pick passes endpoint ID to the loopback config.
- Mac: first option is really 'All system audio', broader than Linux/Windows 'Default output'. Picking a device changes meaning to 'only audio routed to that device' (device-specific tap; unproven).
- Label mismatch to resolve: per-platform labels, or make Linux/Windows 'All' real (one capture per sink/device + mix).

Multi-select (N devices) option, beyond this bead's single-pick scope:
- audioTargetSinkName string -> list, with config migration on load.
- Input-side mixer summing N streams before feature extraction; sample-rate mismatch handling (resample vs per-stream).
- Mac: N device taps + aggregates; Windows: N loopback devices; Linux: N captures or a PipeWire combine sink.
- Store stable IDs (WASAPI endpoint ID, CoreAudio UID), not names; decide missing-device behavior (Linux silently falls back today, Aurora-4xq).
- Rough cost: ~+1 day over the single-pick 2-3 day estimate. Suggestion floated (not decided): single-pick first.
- Per-app capture (Mac process list tap; Windows process loopback, one tree per client) noted as a separate, larger feature; out of scope.

title: Mac (optional): prove the bundle needs no Homebrew via sandbox-exec
description: Stronger than the DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES count done in qy5.6. Launch the bundled app under 'sandbox-exec -p "(version 1)(allow default)(deny file-read* (subpath \"/opt/homebrew\"))"' and confirm it starts and serves the WebUI. sandbox-exec is deprecated but works. Confirms enforcement, not just observation. Not a substitute for a genuinely Homebrew-free Mac.
acceptance_criteria: Bundled app (from tools/mac/bundle-dylibs.sh) launches and answers GET /api/hue/connection with /opt/homebrew reads denied; the unbundled build fails the same test (negative control).
notes: PASSED 2026-09-29. Profile: (version 1)(allow default)(deny file-read* (subpath "/opt/homebrew"))(deny file-read-metadata ...); sanity: 'ls /opt/homebrew/lib' under it -> Operation not permitted. Bundled copy (bundle-dylibs.sh output, hardened + Aurora.entitlements) launched under sandbox-exec and answered GET /api/hue/connection on :8215. Negative control (plain build/mac-app copy) aborted in dyld: Library not loaded /opt/homebrew/opt/aubio/lib/libaubio.5.dylib. So the bundle does not need Homebrew at runtime, enforced not just observed. Caveats: deny is on Homebrew paths only (not a clean Mac; /usr/local etc. untouched); sandbox-exec is deprecated; only a launch + one REST call, not a full capture run.
close_reason: Bundled app runs with /opt/homebrew reads denied; unbundled control fails in dyld.
